target_customer: Developers and platforms needing to detect AI-generated images and deepfakes
problem: Distinguishing AI-generated images from real ones is increasingly hard. Aedilic released Nonescape, an open source model for detection, and also operated GPUDeploy, a GPU rental marketplace.
business_model: Open source detection models with unclear monetization; GPU marketplace take rate for GPUDeploy

founders.name: Nicholas Waltz
education: University of Cambridge, Master's in Econometrics
founders.background_notes: Per YC launch post; research on random forests and DBSCAN.

founders.name: Lukas Schneider
education: ETH Zurich, MSc Robotics, Automation and Control
founders.background_notes: Per YC page and launch post; wrote the RSL open source reinforcement learning library.

competitors.name: Reality Defender
competitors.what: Detection of deepfakes across image, audio, video and text
competitors.funding_then: 15M dollar Series A led by DCVC in October 2023

technical_complexity.rationale: Generalizable detection of images from new diffusion and GAN models is an arms race needing continuous retraining, hard for two people.

defensibility.rationale: The model was open source under Apache 2.0 so anyone could copy it, and detectors go stale as generators change.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Specialist vendors and platforms offered detection. No source ties this to Aedilic's fate.

market_need_then: Deepfake detection attracted funding by late 2023, shown by the Reality Defender round, but no demand data for Aedilic was found.

branding.domain_note: Product site nonescape.com did not resolve at fetch time.

brand_strength.rationale: Company name Aedilic is obscure and the products ran under other names (Nonescape, GPUDeploy), so no single brand formed. No press found.

pivots.from: GPUDeploy GPU rental marketplace (Airbnb for GPUs)
pivots.why: Not stated; the YC launch post covers only GPUDeploy and the YC description covers only detection, so the order and reason are unclear

outcome_analysis: YC lists Aedilic as inactive with a detection product that differs from its only launch post, a GPU marketplace. No shutdown notice or cause was found, so the cause is not public. The split between two products with different markets suggests an unfocused path, but no source states that.
notes: nonescape.com failed DNS at fetch. The $500K figure rests on one company database (TheCompanyCheck), which also mislabels the business as drone delivery in Palo Alto, so it is unreliable; the date is unknown. Hugging Face page lists Aedilic Inc as developer. The pivot direction is unverified. Founders' details come from the YC page and launch post.
